docs.title: Chart tool
docs.text:
The Chart tool opens the chart designer with the current Query Tool result. It supports chart selection, series definitions, labels, formatting, filters, and returning chart definitions to Excel or Canvas.

A detailed chart guide will document the individual chart types and their formatting options.

Return to Statistics and charts in Query Tool.

docs.title: Mini DAX and measures
docs.text:
Mini DAX is QReports' focused expression engine for measures and calculated columns. The Measures ribbon command and the Canvas Measures command open the WebView Measure workspace. It is used by matrices, charts, Canvas visuals, and QReports table output. It is not the same thing as sending a full DAX query to the Excel Power Pivot model.

The workspace places source Fields on the left, saved measures/calculated columns beside them, and the name, expandable expression editor, validation status, matrix wells, and result preview in the main area. The two list panes and matrix result can be resized or collapsed. Load data runs the source query with its current QReports parameters; measures remain editable before data is loaded.

When the Query Web connection is model, it can run normal model queries. The formulas on this page are the smaller Mini DAX formulas managed in Measure workspace.

docs.title: Measure or calculated column?
docs.text:
Type Evaluation context Typical use Measure Evaluated after dimensions and filters establish a group. Totals, averages, ratios, prior-period values, rank. Calculated column Evaluated once for each source row before grouping. Categories, cleaned text, date parts, row calculations.

Calculated columns cannot reference aggregate measures and cannot call aggregate or context functions such as SUM, CALCULATE, ALL, or REMOVEFILTERS.

docs.title: Basic syntax
docs.text:
The editor stores the output name separately from the formula. For a measure named Margin, enter:

DIVIDE(SUM(Profit), SUM(Revenue))

Mini DAX supports arithmetic, comparisons, AND, OR, variables, and comments:

VAR _revenue = SUM(Revenue)
VAR _profit = SUM(Profit)
RETURN
    IF(_revenue = 0, BLANK(), DIVIDE(_profit, _revenue))

Comments begin with //. Names are matched without case sensitivity. Use Ctrl+Space or begin typing to display available names.

docs.title: Aggregate functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax Description SUM SUM(column [, filter]) Sum numeric values in context. AVERAGE / AVG AVERAGE(column [, filter]) Average numeric values. MIN MIN(column [, filter]) Minimum value. MAX MAX(column [, filter]) Maximum value. COUNT COUNT(column [, filter]) Count non-blank values. DISTINCTCOUNT DISTINCTCOUNT(column) Count distinct non-blank values. SELECTEDVALUE SELECTEDVALUE(column [, alternate]) Single value in context, otherwise alternate or blank.

An optional aggregate filter is a simple row condition:

SUM(Revenue, Month = 1)

docs.title: Math and ranking
docs.text:
Function Syntax Description DIVIDE DIVIDE(numerator, denominator) Safe division; zero returns blank. ROUND ROUND(number, digits) Round halves away from zero. ROUNDUP ROUNDUP(number, digits) Round away from zero. ROUNDDOWN ROUNDDOWN(number, digits) Round towards zero. NEGATE / NEG NEGATE(number) Reverse the sign. REVERSE_SIGN REVERSE_SIGN(number) Synonym for NEGATE. RANK RANK(value [, ASC|DESC] [, DENSE|SKIP]) Rank the aggregated matrix values.

RANK runs after aggregation:

RANK(Sales_total, DESC, DENSE)

docs.title: Logical functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax Description IF IF(condition, trueValue [, falseValue]) Return one of two expressions. SWITCH SWITCH(expression, value1, result1, ... [, else]) Choose from alternatives. BLANK BLANK() Return a blank value. TRUE TRUE() Logical true. FALSE FALSE() Logical false. 
SWITCH(
    TRUE(),
    Margin < 0, "Loss",
    Margin < 0.1, "Low",
    Margin < 0.25, "Medium",
    "High"
)

docs.title: Text functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax FORMAT FORMAT(value, "format") CONCATENATE CONCATENATE(value1, value2, ...) CONTAINSSTRING CONTAINSSTRING(text, findText) UPPER UPPER(text) LOWER LOWER(text) LEFT LEFT(text, count) RIGHT RIGHT(text, count) MID MID(text, start, count)

MID uses a one-based start. The & operator can also concatenate text.

CONCATENATE(UPPER(Region), " - ", FORMAT(SUM(Sales), "#,##0"))

docs.title: Date functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax Description YEAR YEAR(date) Extract year. MONTH MONTH(date) Extract month. WEEK WEEK(date) Culture-based week number. TODAY TODAY() Current local date. DATEFROMPARTS DATEFROMPARTS(year, month, day) Construct a date. DATEOFFSET DATEOFFSET(date, years, months, days, weeks) Shift a date.

Calculated-column examples:

DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(InvoiceDate), MONTH(InvoiceDate), 1)

DATEOFFSET(InvoiceDate, -1, 0, 0, 0)

docs.title: Filter context with CALCULATE
docs.text:
CALCULATE reevaluates a supported aggregate after changing simple column filters:

CALCULATE(SUM(Cost), Year = 2025)

Use REMOVEFILTERS or ALL inside CALCULATE to remove selected dimension filters:

VAR _currentYear = MAX(Year)
RETURN
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Cost),
        REMOVEFILTERS(Year),
        Year = _currentYear - 1
    )

Here, ALL(column) and REMOVEFILTERS(column) only remove that column's current filter inside CALCULATE; they do not return general-purpose DAX table expressions.

docs.title: Parameters in formulas
docs.text:
QReports patches parameter tokens before compiling a formula:

CALCULATE(
    SUM(Revenue),
    Year = {{pyear}}
)

Use a raw numeric parameter for pyear. For text comparisons, use DAX string parsing or provide quotes through the parameter definition.

docs.title: Average price
docs.text:
VAR _amount = SUM(Amount)
VAR _quantity = SUM(Quantity)
RETURN DIVIDE(_amount, _quantity)

docs.title: Growth percentage
docs.text:
IF(
    PriorYear = 0,
    BLANK(),
    DIVIDE(CurrentYear - PriorYear, PriorYear)
)

docs.title: Row-level category
docs.text:
Create a calculated column and enter:

IF(Amount < 0, "Credit", "Debit")

docs.title: Differences from full DAX
docs.text:
Mini DAX is intentionally smaller than Microsoft DAX:

  • it evaluates QReports table/matrix data, not a semantic model with relationships;
  • it is an expression engine, not the DAX query language—EVALUATE and DEFINE belong to model mode;
  • iterator and table functions such as SUMX, FILTER, ADDCOLUMNS, SUMMARIZE, and RELATED are not implemented;
  • there is no full relationship propagation or Power Pivot storage engine;
  • CALCULATE supports focused column comparisons plus ALL/REMOVEFILTERS, not every DAX filter expression;
  • time-intelligence functions such as SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR, DATESYTD, and DAX DATEADD are not included; use DATEOFFSET and explicit filters;
  • RANK is a QReports post-aggregation operation, not RANKX;
  • blanks use an internal representation and may render as empty output;
  • number, week, and date formatting can depend on the current Windows culture.

If a formula requires model relationships, iterators, or advanced time intelligence, use a real Power Pivot measure instead. Query Tool's Power Pivot menu links to Excel's model tools.

Return to the Query Tool guide.

docs.title: Formula Helper
docs.text:
Formula Helper is the reference and code-generation pane for QRep Excel Code. It helps you find a keyword, supply valid options, preview the resulting syntax, and insert it into Excel.

It is not intended to be the primary tutorial for the language. Start with QRep Excel Code to understand how connection, query, and output rows work together, then use Formula Helper while building a report.

docs.title: Open the helper
docs.text: Choose QRep > Formula Helper to show or hide the pane on the right side of Excel. The pane stays close to the worksheet so you can inspect a report definition and insert generated code at the active cell.

docs.title: Choose what to create
docs.text:
The workflow selector organizes the supported builders into four groups.

Mode Available templates Report output Table, Dynamic table, Pivot table, Summary, Subtotal Companion row Column / measure row, Crossfilter row, Parameter row Control setup Parameter setting, Template report setup, Sheet password Raw keyword Direct access to the available keyword definitions

Selecting a template displays a short explanation, a structure preview, and only the options relevant to that keyword.

docs.title: Look up reference information
docs.text:
Use the reference browser and search box when you need to check a function, option, filter operator, or example. This is the quickest use of Formula Helper: look up the exact syntax without leaving Excel or changing the current worksheet definition.

The helper can also load the active Excel definition, making it easier to inspect or adjust code that is already present.

docs.title: Generate report output code
docs.text:
The output builders produce correctly ordered options for:

  • table, including group, filter, sort, options, and top rows;
  • dtable, for structured Excel table output;
  • ptable, for pivot-style output;
  • summary, for compact value and measure rows;
  • subtotal, including groups, filters, sorting, and outline options.

For example, selecting Report output > Dynamic table and entering a group, filter, and row limit can produce:

dtable;group(continent);filter(year=2026);toprows(20)

The generated syntax is shown in the preview before it is inserted.

docs.title: Table helper
docs.text:
The dedicated table helper is designed for complete table definitions, not only the first keyword cell. Use it to:

  • choose output fields and their order;
  • assign aggregations and display labels;
  • create an explicit header row;
  • create footer values such as $sum, $count, and $avg;
  • add footer labels and outline behavior;
  • preview the worksheet structure before insertion.

An inserted template can look like this:

ABCD 7table;group(continent)continentpopulation 8+headerCONTINENTPOPULATION 9+footer;outlinelabel(SUMMARY)$sum

docs.title: Subtotal helper
docs.text:
Use the subtotal helper to generate hierarchical output without manually assembling every template row. It supports grouping levels, selected measures, labels, headers and footers, Excel outline behavior, and initially collapsed groups.

Preview the structure before insertion. Check that the grouping order runs from the outer group to the detailed level and that aggregate values are placed in the intended output columns.

docs.title: Companion rows
docs.text:
The Column / measure row builder supports field or measure names, filters, aggregation, units, labels, and options. Its aggregation choices include SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, FIRST, and LAST.

The Crossfilter row builder creates per-column filters. The Parameter row builder creates parameter/value pairs for report code.

docs.title: Control-sheet setup
docs.text:
The Control setup mode generates rows intended for _control:

Template Generated purpose Parameter setting set | parameter | value | user input | advanced JSON Template report setup setreport | template | report | parameter/value pairs Sheet password setpassword | sheet | password

For advanced parameter input types, list lookups, tree levels, formatting, text parsing, and sheet scope, use Parameter Manager after creating the base setting. See Parameters.

docs.title: Insert safely
docs.text:
1. Select the target cell or existing definition in Excel.
  2. Choose the mode and template.
  3. Fill in the displayed options.
  4. Review the syntax or worksheet preview.
  5. Use Insert into Excel only after confirming the active position.
  6. Load the selected line to test the result.

Use Load from Excel when modifying an existing definition. This reduces the risk of recreating options that are already stored in the worksheet.

docs.title: Run a query
docs.text:
1. Open Excel and select the QReports ribbon.
  2. Open the Query Tool.
  3. Select or configure a connection.
  4. Enter a query and preview the result.
  5. Return the result to the active workbook.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Learn how the worksheet definition is assembled in QRep Excel Code.
  • Use Formula Helper to look up syntax and generate table or subtotal code.
  • Use Mini SQL to query Excel tables without an external database.
  • Add parameters to make a report interactive.
  • Add Mini DAX measures or calculated columns before returning data.
  • Save the workbook with its QReports definitions.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Microsoft Excel for Windows
  • .NET Framework 4.8
  • Visual Studio Tools for Office Runtime

docs.title: Install QReports
docs.text:
1. Close Excel.
  2. Download and run setup.exe.
  3. Complete the installation prompts.
  4. Open Excel and confirm that the QReports ribbon is visible.

QReports checks the installation site for published updates.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text: Close and reopen Excel after a new release has been published. Follow the update prompt if one appears.

docs.title: Mini SQL for Excel tables
docs.text:
Mini SQL is QReports' in-memory query language for Excel tables and delimited files. It provides a familiar SQL-shaped way to filter, join, group, calculate, and sort tabular data without first loading it into an external database.

Mini SQL is used when Conn is set to table and for saved CSV/TEXT file connections. The same engine is also used for published Canvas tables.

docs.title: First query
docs.text:
Assume the workbook contains Excel tables named country and continent:

SELECT
    continent,
    SUM(population) AS population_total
FROM country
WHERE year = 2025
GROUP BY continent
ORDER BY population_total DESC

To run it:

  1. Open Query Tool.
  2. Select table from Conn.
  3. Select Table to list workbook tables.
  4. Enter the Mini SQL statement.
  5. Select Run or press F5.

Table and column names come from Excel table names and headers, not worksheet names or cell addresses.

docs.title: Supported statement shape
docs.text:
Mini SQL supports one SELECT statement with the following general shape:

SELECT [TOP number]
    expression [AS alias], ...
FROM table [alias]
[INNER | LEFT | RIGHT | FULL [OUTER]] JOIN table [alias] ON condition
[WHERE condition]
[GROUP BY column, ...]
[HAVING condition]
[ORDER BY expression [ASC | DESC], ...]

Supported query features include:

  • SELECT * for ordinary, non-aggregated projections;
  • column aliases with AS;
  • table aliases;
  • TOP n;
  • inner, left, right, and full joins;
  • WHERE comparisons using =, <>, <, >, <=, and >=;
  • AND, OR, IN (...), BETWEEN, LIKE, IS NULL, and IS NOT NULL;
  • GROUP BY, aggregate expressions, and HAVING;
  • ORDER BY ... ASC and ORDER BY ... DESC;
  • CASE WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE ... END;
  • QReports parameters such as {{pyear}}.

With grouping or aggregate expressions, list every required non-aggregate output column in GROUP BY. SELECT * is not supported in an aggregate query.

docs.title: Joins and aliases
docs.text:
Aliases make joins easier to read and prevent ambiguous column names:

SELECT
    c.country_name,
    c.continent_code,
    g.continent_name,
    c.population
FROM country c
LEFT JOIN continent g
    ON c.continent_code = g.continent_code
WHERE c.population > 1000000
ORDER BY c.population DESC

Join conditions should use column equality or other straightforward comparisons. Mini SQL is intended for table-shaped reporting logic; highly nested database join expressions should remain in the source database.

docs.title: Filters and parameters
docs.text:
SELECT country_name, year, population
FROM country
WHERE year BETWEEN 2020 AND 2025
  AND continent_code IN ('EU', 'NA')
  AND country_name LIKE 'N%'
  AND population IS NOT NULL

String literals use single quotes. A single quote inside a value is doubled: 'O''Brien'.

Parameters are resolved before Mini SQL runs:

SELECT country_name, population
FROM country
WHERE year = {{pyear}}
  AND {{continent}}

If continent produces continent IN ('Europe','Asia'), the parsed statement is valid Mini SQL. Use Query > Parse query to inspect the exact result.

docs.title: Aggregate functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax Purpose COUNT COUNT(column) Count non-null values. COUNTDISTINCT COUNTDISTINCT(column) Count distinct non-null values. SUM SUM(column) Sum numeric values. AVG AVG(column) Average numeric values. MIN MIN(column) Minimum value. MAX MAX(column) Maximum value. CONCAT CONCAT(column [, delimiter]) Join unique text values; comma is the default delimiter. 
SELECT
    continent,
    COUNTDISTINCT(country_code) AS countries,
    SUM(population) AS population,
    CONCAT(country_name, ', ') AS country_list
FROM country
GROUP BY continent
HAVING SUM(population) > 100000000
ORDER BY population DESC

docs.title: String functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax Example SUBSTRING SUBSTRING(text, start, length) SUBSTRING(country_name, 1, 3) LENGTH LENGTH(text) LENGTH(country_name) REPLACE REPLACE(text, find, replacement) REPLACE(code, '-', '') TRIM TRIM(text) TRIM(country_name) LEFT LEFT(text, length) LEFT(account, 3) RIGHT RIGHT(text, length) RIGHT(account, 2) UPPER UPPER(text) UPPER(country_name) LOWER LOWER(text) LOWER(country_name) FORMAT FORMAT(value, format) FORMAT(amount, '#,##0.00')

SUBSTRING uses a one-based start position. FORMAT returns text and uses the current Windows culture.

docs.title: Date functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax Notes GETDATE GETDATE() Current local date and time. TODAY TODAY() Current local date with no time. XLDATE XLDATE(value) Convert an Excel serial value to a date. XLDATETIME XLDATETIME(value) Convert an Excel serial value to date and time. DATEADD DATEADD(interval, number, date) Day, month, year, hour, minute, or second. DATEDIFF DATEDIFF(interval, date1, date2) Day, hour, minute, or second. YEAR YEAR(date) Extract the year. MONTH MONTH(date) Extract the month number. DATEPART DATEPART(part, date) Day, month, year, quarter, week, or weekday. 
SELECT
    invoice_date,
    YEAR(invoice_date) AS invoice_year,
    DATEADD(month, 1, invoice_date) AS next_month,
    FORMAT(invoice_date, 'yyyy-MM-dd') AS date_text
FROM invoices

docs.title: Logical, numeric, and conversion functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax Purpose CASE CASE WHEN condition THEN value ELSE value END Conditional output. IIF IIF(condition, trueValue, falseValue) Inline condition. COALESCE COALESCE(value1, value2, ...) First non-null value. ISNULL ISNULL(value, replacement) Replace a null. ROUND ROUND(number, decimals) Round to decimal places. FLOOR FLOOR(number) Round down. CEILING CEILING(number) Round up. ABS ABS(number) Absolute value. MOD MOD(dividend, divisor) Division remainder. CAST CAST(expression, 'datatype') Convert to a supported type.

Supported CAST targets include integer, long, double, decimal, text, date, datetime, and Boolean aliases. Mini SQL uses CAST(value, 'INT'), not SQL Server's CAST(value AS INT) syntax.

CONVERT may appear in function-help metadata in some builds, but the Mini SQL evaluator currently implements CAST. Prefer CAST for portable QReports definitions.

docs.title: Differences from database SQL
docs.text:
Mini SQL deliberately does not try to be a full database server:

  • it operates on in-memory table data and has no database indexes or query optimizer;
  • it supports one SELECT, not INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, or stored procedures;
  • CTEs, subqueries, UNION, window functions, and database-specific syntax are not supported;
  • use TOP n; LIMIT and OFFSET are not part of the parser;
  • schema-qualified database names are not relevant to workbook table mode;
  • function coverage and null/type conversion rules are smaller than in a database;
  • very large workbooks can use substantial memory because source tables are materialized;
  • culture can affect text-to-number, date parsing, and FORMAT output;
  • database permissions, transactions, indexes, and execution plans do not apply.

Use Mini SQL when the source is already in Excel and the transformation is report-sized. Use a named database connection when the source is large, the SQL is complex, or filtering and aggregation should happen on the server.

docs.title: CSV and delimited text files
docs.text:
Create a CSV or TEXT connection in Connection Manager and select the source file. Configure separator, whether the first row contains headers, and encoding. Quoted fields are supported.

The source appears using a normalized version of its filename. The stable alias data is also available, which avoids problems when a filename contains spaces or punctuation:

SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS amount
FROM data
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY amount DESC

Delimited values are initially read as text. Use the Mini SQL conversion functions when numeric or date interpretation is required, and verify separators/encoding if the preview produces an unexpected number of columns.

Return to the Query Tool guide.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameters let users change queries, Mini SQL, Mini DAX, API definitions, charts, and Canvas content without editing the underlying text. Definitions are managed in Parameter Manager; user-enabled values appear in the simpler Parameter Input form.

docs.title: Add and order parameters
docs.text:
1. Open Parameters from the QRep Ribbon or select Param in Query Tool.
  2. Open the advanced manager if Parameter Input is shown first.
  3. Select Add.
  4. Enter the parameter name and current value.
  5. Choose an input type and configure its tabs.
  6. Check User input if report users should change it.
  7. Select Save.

Parameter names are referenced as {{name}}. Keep names short and avoid punctuation that could be confused with a property reference.

The order in Parameter Manager controls Parameter Input. Right-click the list to move a parameter Up, Down, First, or Last. The UI checkbox column identifies parameters with User input enabled; click the checkbox directly to enable or disable it.

For Manual list and SQL list parameters, Pick opens the configured selector. The popup uses single selection, checked multi-selection, or a hierarchical tree as appropriate and shows the current selection before it is applied.

docs.title: Parameter Manager layout
docs.text:
The editor is divided into tabs so that only settings relevant to the selected input type are shown:

Tab What it controls When it appears Setup Input type, user input, blank/multi-select behavior, manual values, sheet scope, list height, and expanding lists. Always. Lookup Connection, lookup query, value/display columns, and tree-level columns. List inputs; the lookup fields are required for SQL list. Text parsing Prefix/postfix, None handling, item encapsulation, and separator. Always. Format Date format or numeric minimum, maximum, increment, and number format. Date picker or Numeric input only.

The blue i buttons beside Manual list, Tree level columns, and Text parsing open short examples without changing the parameter. They are useful as an in-form syntax reference.

docs.title: Common fields
docs.text: Field Purpose Name Stable token name, for example pyear. Current value Current raw value or first selected lookup value. Default value Fallback when no current value exists. Display name Label shown to the user. Description Help text below the input control. User input Include the parameter in Parameter Input. Allow blank Permit an empty selected value. Multi select Permit more than one list value. Sheet scope Restrict visibility to selected worksheets; no selection means all sheets.

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
Use Text for free-form input such as a year, account code, or search term.

WHERE fiscal_year = {{pyear}}

For numeric text, use Raw text parsing. For a SQL text value, choose SQL string so Europe becomes 'Europe'.

docs.title: Manual list
docs.text:
Use Manual list when choices are stable and do not need a query. Enter comma-separated items, one item per line, or value/display pairs supported by the editor.

EU=Europe
NA=North America
AS=Asia

The stored value can be EU while the user sees Europe.

For a hierarchical multi-select list, enable Hierarchical tree list and enter one complete path per line. Separate levels with >; the final segment is the selectable leaf:

Europe > Western Europe > BE=Belgium
Europe > Nordics > NO=Norway
Asia > East Asia > JP=Japan

This creates Continent → Region → Country. Selecting a parent selects or clears every leaf beneath it. Any number of parent levels is supported. Existing comma-, semicolon-, and newline-separated flat lists remain valid.

For a tree, keep each complete path on its own physical line. Use value=display only on the final leaf when the stored value and caption differ. For example, NO is inserted into the query while Norway is shown to the user. Commas and semicolons are intended for flat lists, not as hierarchy markers.

docs.title: SQL list
docs.text:
Use SQL list when choices should be loaded from a connection or Excel table.

The Manual list box is disabled for SQL lists. A lookup connection and lookup SQL must be configured before the parameter can be saved.

Configure:

  • Lookup connection: named database connection, table, or another supported source;
  • Lookup SQL: query returning lookup rows;
  • Value column: value inserted into the query;
  • Display column: friendly text shown in Parameter Input;
  • Hierarchical tree list: show multiple parent levels;
  • Tree level columns: comma-separated result columns from root to parent;
  • List height: minimum height of the list control.
  • Expand height: let the multi-select list or tree use additional vertical space when Parameter Input is resized.

Example lookup:

SELECT
    Region,
    Continent,
    CountryCode,
    CountryName
FROM country
ORDER BY Continent, Region, CountryName

For Continent → Region → Country:

  • Value column: CountryCode
  • Display column: CountryName
  • Tree level columns: Continent, Region

The value/display columns form the lowest leaf. Checking or clearing a parent checks or clears all descendants. Tree selection is intended for multi-select lists.

If several parameters have Expand height enabled, only the first eligible multi-select list in Parameter Manager order expands. Parameters above it remain anchored to the top, while parameters below it remain anchored to the bottom. Reorder parameters in Parameter Manager to choose which list receives the extra space.

docs.title: Pick and verify list values
docs.text:
Select Pick... in Parameter Manager to test the configured list before saving:

  • a single-select parameter shows one selectable value;
  • Multi select shows checkboxes;
  • Allow blank adds a (Blank) choice;
  • the configurable None caption is shown as the first None choice;
  • a hierarchical list shows expandable parent nodes;
  • checking or clearing a parent applies the same state to all leaves below it;
  • the selection summary above the list shows the values currently selected.

The picker respects the same configuration used by Parameter Input, including value/display columns and tree levels. Selecting OK updates the current parameter selection in the manager; select Save to persist it.

docs.title: Date picker
docs.text:
Use Date picker to show a calendar control. On Format, set the output format. yyyy-MM-dd turns 21 August 2026 into:

2026-08-21

Combine it with SQL string parsing when the source expects:

WHERE order_date = '2026-08-21'

docs.title: Numeric input
docs.text:
Use Numeric input for a spinner control. On Format, configure minimum, maximum, and increment—for example 1, 10, or 1000.

The Number format controls the text produced by the parameter. It accepts .NET numeric formats, including:

Format Example for 1234.5 N0 1,234 # 1235 0.00 1234.50 #,##0.## 1,234.5

Formatting affects the parameter text sent to SQL, Mini SQL, DAX, APIs, and Canvas queries, so choose a format accepted by the target source.

The Format tab appears only for Date picker and Numeric input. Lookup appears only for a list input.

docs.title: Sheet scope
docs.text:
No checked worksheet means the parameter is available on every sheet. Check one or more sheets to restrict it.

Example: accountid scoped to Sheet1 appears when the input form is opened for Sheet1, but not Sheet2.

Right-click the sheet list and use Select all or Clear all. Clear all restores the default all-sheets behavior.

docs.title: Text parsing
docs.text: Text parsing controls the exact replacement string. Input type is selected only on Setup; there is no second input-type box here.

docs.title: Scalar modes
docs.text:
Mode Raw value Result Raw text Europe Europe SQL string Europe 'Europe' DAX string Europe "Europe"

Quotes inside values are escaped for the selected string mode.

docs.title: Prefix and suffix around the complete value
docs.text:
With Pre value costcenter=', raw value 100, and Post value ', the result is:

costcenter='100'

Keep parsing as Raw text here because the prefix and suffix already supply quotes.

docs.title: Multi-value formatting
docs.text:
For values 100, 200, and 300:

Setting Value Pre value costcenter IN ( Separator , Encapsulation prefix ' Encapsulation suffix ' Post value )

Result:

costcenter IN ('100','200','300')

Escapes such as \n and \t are decoded in parsing fields.

Select the i button on Text parsing for a compact explanation of Pre value, Post value, None representation, per-item encapsulation, and Separator. The example line at the bottom of the tab previews how the current settings are concatenated.

docs.title: None selection
docs.text:
List inputs can offer None. The None representation is emitted instead of values. A common SQL representation is:

1=1

None caption controls what the user sees. It defaults to (None), but can be changed to (All), No filter, or another suitable caption. The caption is only presentation text; None representation remains the value inserted into the query.

Place this parameter where a complete condition belongs:

WHERE {{continent}}

Do not use WHERE continent = {{continent}} with 1=1, because it produces invalid logic.

docs.title: Parameter references
docs.text:
The normal token resolves the formatted value:

{{continent}}
{{continent.Value}}

Additional properties:

Reference Result {{name.Display}} Formatted display value(s). {{name.Current}} Current scalar value. {{name.CurrentDisplay}} Current display scalar. {{name.Default}} Default value. {{name.Name}} Normalized name. {{name.DisplayName}} or {{name.Label}} User-facing label. {{name.Description}} Description text. {{name.Count}} Number of selected raw values. {{name.Separator}} Multi-value separator. {{name.Prefix}} Per-item encapsulation prefix. {{name.Suffix}} Per-item encapsulation suffix.

Names and properties are case-insensitive.

docs.title: Parameter Input
docs.text:
Only parameters marked User input and matching the current sheet scope are shown.

The form grows when list controls require more vertical space. List height is a minimum; screen space can constrain the final window.

  • Save stores values without refreshing the report.
  • Save and Load stores all parameters, recalculates dependent workbook formulas, and loads the active report sheet.
  • Cancel closes without applying pending edits.

Pending control edits are committed before Save; pressing Tab after typing is not required.

docs.title: The _control worksheet
docs.text:
Excel-hosted parameters are persisted as set rows on _control.

Column Content A Keyword set. B Normalized parameter name. C Current resolved value or an existing Excel formula. D TRUE for user input; blank/false otherwise. E Compact JSON with advanced settings.

Column E can contain display text, selections, input type, lookup definition, hierarchy, list height, scope, parsing, date format, and numeric limits. Older simple set rows remain compatible.

The saved JSON also retains the None caption, number format, expanding-list option, current display values, and hierarchical tree-level settings. Reopening Parameter Manager reconstructs these controls from column E rather than relying only on the formatted value in column C.

docs.title: Formula-driven parameters
docs.text:
For a non-user-input parameter, an existing formula in column C is preserved. This allows the value to depend on other cells or parameters:

=TEXT(C2,"0000")

For a user-input parameter, saving writes the user's selected resolved value directly to column C. The input form is the source of that value.

Save and Load writes the rows and waits for workbook calculation so formulas depending on the changed parameter are updated before report loading continues.

docs.title: Generate reports with setreport
docs.text: setreport creates one or more report sheets from a reusable template sheet. It is useful when the report layout is identical but each generated sheet needs different parameter values, such as one sheet per company, region, period, or department.

docs.title: Column layout
docs.text:
Column Content A Keyword setreport. B Name of the template worksheet. C Name of the report worksheet to create. D First parameter name. E First parameter value. F Second parameter name. G Second parameter value. H/I onward Additional parameter name/value pairs.

The parameter columns always occur in pairs: name, value, name, value. Parameter names refer to set rows on _control. If a named parameter does not yet have a set row, QReports can create the missing value row while processing the report.

docs.title: Example: several reports from one template
docs.text:
The following setup creates three sheets from Regional template. Each generated report temporarily receives its own continent and pyear values.

ABCDEFG 2setcontinentEuropeTRUE 3setpyear2026TRUE 5setreportRegional templateReport EuropecontinentEuropepyear2026 6setreportRegional templateReport AmericascontinentNorth Americapyear2026 7setreportRegional templateReport AsiacontinentAsiapyear2026

The template can contain normal QRep Excel Code, parameter references such as {{continent}}, formatting, formulas, charts, and Canvas shapes. The template may be hidden; QReports temporarily makes it available while copying and restores its previous visibility afterward.

docs.title: Create or refresh generated sheets
docs.text:
1. Create the template sheet and test it with ordinary parameter values.
  2. Add one setreport row for every report sheet required.
  3. Select QRep > Load selected.
  4. Find the generated entries in the dialog. Their action is shown as From template, even when the target sheet does not exist yet.
  5. Select the required reports and choose Load selected.

For each selected row, QReports applies that row's parameter pairs, copies the template, names the copy using column C, and loads all QRep blocks on the generated sheet. The previous global parameter values are restored after that report finishes.

docs.title: Important behavior
docs.text:
• If the generated report sheet already exists, it is deleted and recreated from the template. Do not store manual changes only on a generated sheet.
  • The template and report sheet names must be different.
  • _control cannot be used as the generated report name.
  • Every generated report name should be unique.
  • Keep the source layout and formulas in the template; keep report-specific values in the setreport pairs.
  • The same template can be reused by any number of setreport rows.

Formula Helper can generate the base row using Control setup > Template report setup.

docs.title: Manual-editing cautions
docs.text:
• Keep column A as set.
  • Keep parameter names unique.
  • Do not edit column E unless you can repair JSON.
  • A formula in column C should normally have User input disabled.
  • Saving Parameter Manager removes stale rows for parameters deleted from the manager.

docs.title: Example: scoped tree lookup
docs.text:
Goal: choose countries only on Regional report and create a SQL condition.

  1. Name it country.
  2. Enable User input and Multi select.
  3. Choose SQL list.
  4. Return Continent, Region, CountryCode, and CountryName.
  5. Use CountryCode as Value and CountryName as Display.
  6. Enable the tree and use Continent, Region as levels.
  7. Use Pre value country_code IN ( and Post value ).
  8. Use a single quote as per-item prefix/suffix and comma as separator.
  9. Select only Regional report in Sheet scope.
  10. Write WHERE {{country}} in the query.

Selecting Norway and Sweden produces:

WHERE country_code IN ('NO','SE')

Use Query > Parse query to verify the final text.

docs.title: A parameter is missing from Parameter Input
docs.text: Check that User input is enabled—the UI column should be checked. Then review Sheet scope. No selected sheets means all sheets; one or more checked sheets restrict the parameter to those sheets.

docs.title: Hierarchy disappears after saving
docs.text: For a manual tree, enable both Multi select and Hierarchical tree list, and use one >-separated path per line. For SQL list, make sure Tree level columns contains valid column names returned by the lookup query. The value and display columns are leaves and should not also be listed as parent levels.

docs.title: Pick shows no SQL-list values
docs.text: SQL list requires both a Lookup connection and Lookup SQL. Run or inspect the lookup query and confirm that Value column, Display column, and every Tree level column exist in the returned table.

docs.title: The query contains only a comma-separated value list
docs.text: Check Text parsing. A SQL condition such as continent IN (...) must normally be supplied through Pre value/Post value and item encapsulation, or written around the parameter token in the query. Use Parse query to inspect the final replacement before loading the report.

docs.title: A dependent control-sheet formula has an old result
docs.text: Use Save and Load, not only Save. Save and Load writes all parameter values, requests workbook recalculation, waits for dependent formulas, and then continues with report loading.

docs.title: PowerPoint add-in
docs.text:
Premium/Pro feature: PowerPoint integration requires the PowerPoint Add-in feature together with the applicable Canvas license.

The QReports PowerPoint add-in brings Canvas reports into slides. It uses the same Canvas editor, Query Tool, Mini SQL, Mini DAX measures, API definitions, charts, and parameters as the Excel add-in. The shared concepts are documented once under Excel add-in and linked from this section.

docs.title: How PowerPoint stores a Canvas
docs.text:
When Canvas returns to PowerPoint, the slide receives a rendered picture. QReports stores the Canvas JSON definition with the picture so the report can be reopened, changed, and rendered again.

Deleting or replacing the picture outside QReports can remove the stored definition. Use Edit Selected or Open in Qanvas tool to maintain it.

docs.title: Shared documentation
docs.text:
PowerPoint does not use a second implementation of the report language. These guides also apply:

  • Query Tool for building source queries;
  • Mini SQL for querying tables and published Canvas data;
  • Mini DAX and measures for measures and calculated columns;
  • Parameters for input controls and text parsing;
  • API tool for API definitions;
  • Chart tool for chart design;
  • Canvas tool for pages, tiles, data, formatting, and refresh behavior.

In PowerPoint, these tools are normally reached through Canvas rather than as separate Ribbon buttons.

docs.title: First report
docs.text:
1. Open a presentation and select the target slide.
  2. Choose QReports > New Canvas.
  3. Build the page using the shared Canvas workflow.
  4. Choose Return in Canvas.
  5. Position and resize the resulting picture on the slide.
  6. Select the picture and use Edit Selected when changes are required.

Continue with the PowerPoint QRep Ribbon and shared tools and concepts.

docs.title: PowerPoint QRep Ribbon
docs.text: The QReports tab in PowerPoint manages Canvas pictures and presentation-level parameters.

docs.title: Canvas group
docs.text: Button What it does New Canvas Opens a new Canvas definition and inserts the returned result on the active slide. Edit Selected Opens the Canvas definition stored with the selected QReports picture and replaces the picture after saving. Load selected Lists Canvas shapes in the presentation and rerenders selected shapes or all shapes. Parameters Opens Parameter Input for presentation-level parameters. Save and Load can refresh all Canvas shapes.

docs.title: Help group
docs.text: Button What it does Help Opens the current QReports help and documentation website in the default browser.

docs.title: Shape context menu
docs.text: Right-click a supported shape, picture, object, or drawing and choose Open in Qanvas tool. QReports checks the selected object for a stored Canvas specification before opening it.

docs.title: Refreshing reports
docs.text:
Use Load selected when source data or parameters have changed but the Canvas layout does not need editing. The selection dialog shows the slide and Canvas names. You can load the checked shapes or all discovered Canvas shapes.

Use Edit Selected when changing the page query, measures, tiles, formatting, or Canvas layout.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
PowerPoint parameters use the same input controls and parsing rules as Excel parameters. They are stored with the active presentation rather than in an Excel _control worksheet.

Selecting Save and Load stores the new values and rerenders all discovered Canvas shapes so their queries and text use the updated parameters.

Continue with Canvas tool or Parameters.

docs.title: Shared tools and concepts
docs.text:
The PowerPoint add-in reuses QReports components documented under Excel add-in. The host-specific difference is how definitions are stored and returned: Excel stores report code in cells and Canvas definitions with workbook shapes; PowerPoint stores Canvas definitions with slide pictures.

Shared area Documentation PowerPoint use Query building Query Tool Opened from Canvas to create page or tile queries. Excel/table queries Mini SQL Queries published Canvas tables and other available table sources. Measures Mini DAX and measures Adds measures and calculated columns used by Canvas visuals. Parameters Parameters Uses the same input controls and parsing; values are stored with the presentation. APIs API tool Builds API definitions used through Query Tool and Canvas. Requires the API feature. Charts Chart tool Designs charts used in Canvas tiles. Visual reports Canvas tool Creates the picture and stored definition returned to a slide.

The worksheet-specific QRep Excel Code, _control sheet, setreport, and Excel Ribbon loading commands apply only to Excel workbooks. Their query, formatting, parameter, and measure concepts can still be relevant when the same editors are opened from Canvas.

docs.title: QRep Excel Code
docs.text:
QRep Excel Code is the worksheet language used to connect to data, run a query, and place the result in Excel. A report block normally has three parts: a connection row, one or more query rows, and an output row.

Use this page to learn the language. Use the Formula Helper when you already know what you want and need to look up syntax or generate a correctly formatted table or subtotal definition.

docs.title: The smallest useful report
docs.text:
This example uses the saved connection named demo, runs a SQL query, and returns a normal report table. The first row tells QRep where the data comes from, rows 2 and 3 contain the query, and row 4 defines the output.

ABCD 1conndemo 2sqlSELECT country, population 3sqlFROM country 4tablecountrypopulation

Select a cell in the block and choose Load selected line, or load the active sheet. QRep reads the definition and writes the result below the output row.

The keyword is placed in column A. Its main value is normally placed in column B. Output columns begin farther to the right, allowing each Excel column to describe one returned field or measure.

docs.title: Connection rows
docs.text:
Put the connection row above the query and output belonging to it.

Keyword Purpose conn Uses a named database connection. Put the saved connection name in column B. model Uses the workbook Power Pivot model. powerquery Uses a supported Power Query connection definition. table Uses Excel tables through Mini SQL. file Uses a supported file source. Put its path or saved definition in column B. api Uses a saved API definition. See the API tool. connspec Uses an advanced connection specification stored as JSON.

Connections are created and maintained from QRep > Connections. The Query Tool can also select a connection and write a valid report definition back to the sheet.

docs.title: Query rows
docs.text:
Use sql, q, or query in column A. Put one query line in column B on each row. Keeping SQL on separate worksheet rows makes it easier to insert, remove, and inspect clauses.

ABC 1connsales 2sqlSELECT region, SUM(amount) AS revenue 3sqlFROM sales 4sqlWHERE order_date >= '{{periodfrom}}' 5sqlGROUP BY region 6tableregion

Aliases returned by SQL can be used as the output field names. Parameters such as {{periodfrom}} are replaced before execution; see Parameters.

docs.title: Output rows
docs.text:
The output keyword controls how QRep places the query result in Excel.

Keyword Result table A normal QRep report area with optional grouping, header, footer, and outline rows. dtable A dynamic structured Excel table. ptable A pivot-style result based on grouped fields. summary One compact summary row, commonly used for KPIs and measures. subtotal Grouped details with headers, footers, spacing, and Excel outline levels. load Loads data using the definition without the normal table presentation.

Charts and Canvas definitions are handled by the Chart tool. DAX and model measures are covered in Mini DAX and measures.

docs.title: Keyword map
docs.text:
The following map shows the worksheet codes you are most likely to encounter. Some are generated by a tool and are normally easier to maintain there than by editing their JSON manually.

Area Codes Purpose Connection conn, model, powerquery, table, file, api, connspec Selects the data source for the report block. Query sql, q, query Adds query text from column B. Measures msr Stores the serialized measure definitions associated with a connection. Output table, dtable, ptable, summary, subtotal, load Selects how the result is returned to Excel. Chart chart, graph Stores chart output and definition data; normally maintained in the Chart tool. Companion column, crossfilter, parameter Describes an output column, applies a per-column filter, or supplies parameter/value pairs. Template + header, + footer, + footer1, + footer2 Adds formatting and summary rows to table or subtotal output. Control set, setreport, setpassword Defines parameters, report-sheet mappings, and protected-sheet loading on _control.

msr, chart definitions, advanced parameter settings, and connspec can contain JSON. Prefer Query Tool, Chart tool, Parameter Manager, or Connection Manager when changing those definitions.

docs.title: Dynamic Excel table
docs.text:
Change the output keyword from table to dtable when the result should be an Excel structured table. Column B supplies the table name.

ABCD 1conndemo 2sqlSELECT country, population 3sqlFROM country 4dtabletblCountrycountrypopulation

Useful output options are appended with semicolons:

  • group(continent,region) groups by fields;
  • filter(year=2026,amount>1000) filters the output;
  • sort(year ASC,region DESC) controls ordering;
  • toprows(20) limits the number of displayed rows;
  • noheader, nocrossfilter, and leftcolumn=4 change output behavior.

For example: dtable;group(continent);filter(year=2026);sort(population DESC);toprows(20).

docs.title: Table headers and footers
docs.text:
Template rows start with + in column A. The template type is placed in column B. Values in a header row override generated field names and options such as noheader. Remove the + header row when no explicit header is wanted.

ABCD 7table;group(continent)continentpopulation 8+headerCONTINENTPOPULATION 9+footer;outlinelabel(SUMMARY)$sum

Common template rows include:

Template Use header Supplies the displayed header text. footer Adds a final footer or summary row. footer1, footer2 Adds footer rows at specific subtotal levels. footer;outline Adds a footer participating in Excel outline grouping. footer;outlinec Adds an initially collapsed outline footer.

Footer cells can use labels such as label(SUMMARY), aggregate shortcuts such as $sum, $count, and $avg, or an Excel formula beginning with =.

docs.title: Subtotal reports
docs.text:
Use subtotal for hierarchical reports. List the grouping fields from the outer level to the detail level. Optional footer rows define what appears at each level.

ABCDE 12subtotal;group(continent,region)continentregionpopulation 13+headerCONTINENTREGIONPOPULATION 14+footer1;outlineclabel(TOTAL)$sum

The Formula Helper has dedicated table and subtotal builders for choosing fields, aggregate functions, labels, header/footer rows, and outline behavior.

docs.title: Column definitions and crossfilters
docs.text:
column defines a field or measure and can add agg(...), label(...), unit(...), filter, and display options. Supported aggregation choices include SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, FIRST, and LAST.

crossfilter is a companion row. Put a filter in each output column that it should affect. The values are written directly, without wrapping them in filter(...).

ABCD 20crossfilteryear=2025year=2026 21summarycolumn;Revenue;agg(SUM);label(2025)column;Revenue;agg(SUM);label(2026)

Filter syntax supports equality, >, >=, <, <=, and <>; | for alternatives; - for ranges; * or % wildcards; and NULL or NOT NULL. Comma-separated conditions are combined with AND.

docs.title: Parameters and control rows
docs.text:
Use {{parameter_name}} in SQL, filters, text, and templates. Parameter definitions are normally stored on the _control sheet:

ABCDE 3setpyear2026TRUE{advanced settings JSON} 4setreportTemplateReportpyear2026 5setpasswordReportpassword

set defines the current value, whether it is user-editable, and optional advanced settings. setreport maps a template sheet to a report sheet with optional parameter pairs. setpassword lets QRep temporarily unprotect and restore a report sheet during loading. See Parameters for the full setup.

docs.title: Recommended workflow
docs.text:
1. Create and test the connection in QRep > Connections.
  2. Build and test the SQL in the Query Tool.
  3. Return the definition to Excel as table, dtable, summary, or another output type.
  4. Add grouping, filters, column definitions, and template rows.
  5. Use the Formula Helper to verify syntax or generate table/subtotal code.
  6. Load the selected line while developing, then load the full sheet.

Generated rows such as xlinsr_tbl belong to the loaded result. Edit the QRep definition rows above them, then reload the report.

docs.title: QRep Ribbon
docs.text: The QRep tab is the main Excel entry point for loading reports and opening QReports tools.

docs.title: Update group
docs.text:
Button What it does Load active sheet Unloads generated report data, reruns QReports blocks on the active sheet, restores protection, and refreshes Canvas shapes. Unload active sheet Removes generated output so the underlying xlquery instructions can be edited. Load selected Opens the sheet-selection dialog and loads selected report sheets. Load selected line Runs only the report block belonging to the selected line/cell.

Use Load active sheet for a normal report refresh and Load selected line while developing one block in a large sheet.

docs.title: Tools group
docs.text:
Button What it does Query Web Opens Query Web using the definition at the active cell. Canvas Web Opens the WebView report designer hosted from the active workbook. This is a Premium/Pro licensed feature. API Web Opens API Web. This is a Pro licensed feature. Measures Opens the WebView Measure workspace without loading data until Load data is selected. Formula Helper Shows or hides the right-side reference and code-generation pane for QRep Excel Code. Connections Opens Connection Manager for database, table, model, and API definitions. Parameters Opens Parameter Input for user-enabled parameters stored on _control. Update datamodel Calls Excel's workbook-wide Refresh All.

Legacy tools contains the previous Query Tool, Qanvas Tool, API Tool, and legacy Load selected command so old and new workflows can be compared during migration.

docs.title: Other group
docs.text:
Button What it does Log Opens the in-memory QReports log. Right-click to clear, copy, save, or select text. Help Opens this documentation site in the default browser. Settings Opens administration and support commands.

The Settings menu contains:

  • AI Prompt Helper: builds a copyable prompt using current Excel and QReports context;
  • Automation (VBA): shows example VBA and the add-in ProgID;
  • Manual install company settings: copies a selected company profile into local company settings;
  • Enter License: stores a license key for the current Windows user;
  • License Status: shows customer, edition, expiry, features, and license path;
  • About: shows version, environment, installation, and diagnostic path information.

docs.title: AI Prompt Helper
docs.text:
Enter the actual problem in Your question / ask, then copy the generated Markdown prompt into ChatGPT or another AI assistant. Auto detect uses the most recently active Query Tool, API Tool, or Canvas window; select a tool explicitly when you want a different reference.

For an Excel-sheet question, the helper can include the selected cells, a nearby QRep block, connection/query information, and the embedded QRep syntax library. Worksheet context includes row numbers, column letters, cell addresses, and Excel formulas rather than only calculated values.

Tool-specific context can include:

  • Query Tool connection mode, query, measures, resolved parameters, typed result columns, and a small data sample;
  • API request specification, typed result columns, and a small data sample;
  • Canvas host, current page/query, selected tile, settings, and Canvas JSON.

Large selections and Canvas definitions are truncated to keep the prompt useful. API credentials and sensitive header values are replaced with [REDACTED]; do not manually add secrets to the question. Keep Include library enabled when asking for QRep worksheet syntax, Mini SQL, Mini DAX, parameters, API definitions, or Canvas model guidance.

docs.title: Shape context menu
docs.text: Right-clicking a supported Excel shape, picture, or drawing object adds Open in Qanvas tool. Use it for workbooks containing QReports Canvas content.

docs.title: Licensing
docs.text:
Connections remain available for configuration, while Query Tool, Qanvas, and API functionality can be enabled or disabled by license features. License Status is the quickest way to inspect the current entitlement.

Continue to QRep Excel Code, Query Tool, Parameters, or Technical information.

docs.title: Query Tool
docs.text:
Query Web is the main workspace for finding data, writing and testing queries, previewing results, and returning a data-source definition to Excel. The current ribbon button opens the WebView workspace; the previous WinForms tool remains available under Legacy tools during the transition. Query Web supports SQL connections, Excel tables, the Power Pivot model, Canvas tables, and API definitions.

The workspace uses three resizable areas: sources and fields on the left, the SQL editor in the upper centre, and results below it. Use the edge buttons to collapse or reopen Sources and Tools. The result area contains Grid, JSON, Parsed SQL, and Messages; execution errors automatically activate Messages.

This page explains the normal workflow first, followed by the individual tools and context menus.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Choose a connection at the top of the Sources pane.
  2. Expand a table to browse its columns.
  3. Select a table to inspect its columns, or write SQL directly in Query.
  4. Add parameters such as {{pyear}} when the query needs user input.
  5. Select Run or press F5 to preview the result. New workspaces default to 1,000 preview rows.
  6. Use Apply query when the result and definition are ready for Excel or the calling Canvas.

Right-click a table to preview its top rows, insert its name, create SELECT *, or create a query from its selected columns. Each table also has Selected → query and View top actions. Column filters can load distinct source values or accept advanced expressions such as in (2023,2024), between, comparisons, like, and null tests.

When Query Tool was opened from Canvas, Statistics, or the API tool, Return sends the query back to that calling window instead.

When returning to Excel, Query Tool writes a worksheet definition that QReports can reload. See QRep Excel Code to understand those rows, or use Formula Helper to look up and generate output syntax.

docs.title: Select or configure a connection
docs.text:
The Conn list controls how the query is interpreted and which tables, columns, functions, and execution engine are available.

Connection Intended use Named SQL connection Query a configured database using SQL. table Query Excel workbook tables using the supported table-query syntax. model Query the workbook's Power Pivot model using DAX. canvas Query tables made available by the current Canvas document. API Work with the API definition returned from API Explorer.

The table connection is a core QReports feature. It runs Mini SQL for Excel tables, including filters, joins, groups, calculations, and parameters directly over workbook tables.

To add or change a named connection:

  1. Open Settings > Connections.
  2. Add or edit the connection details in Connection Manager.
  3. Save the connection.
  4. Return to Query Tool and select it from Conn.

Changing the connection clears the old table and column lookup so metadata from different sources is not mixed. Select Table again to load the new source.

docs.title: Find tables and columns
docs.text:
Select Table to load the table list for the current connection. Selecting a table loads its columns in the adjacent column pane. Double-clicking a column inserts it into the query.

The table search supports both ordinary table-name searches and schema-qualified searches:

  • country searches table names across the available schemas.
  • app. shows tables from the app schema.
  • app.coun shows tables in the app schema whose names match coun.

Use View Top Records from a table's context menu when you want to inspect the source before building a query.

docs.title: Query Wizard
docs.text:
Select Wizard to build a query visually:

  1. Check one or more tables.
  2. Check the columns to return.
  3. Add aliases, filters, sorting, or joins where needed.
  4. Use Show Joins to inspect the table relationships.
  5. Use Import from SQL to bring a supported existing SQL query into the wizard.

The generated query is updated as the wizard selections change. Review it before running, particularly when several joins are involved.

docs.title: Write queries with aliases and IntelliSense
docs.text:
IntelliSense is useful for table names, aliases, columns, model fields, and parameter names. Its toolbar state shows On or Off; it can also be changed through Query > IntelliSense.

Use explicit aliases for readable queries:

SELECT
    c.continent AS Continent,
    SUM(c.population) AS Population
FROM app.country AS c
WHERE c.year = {{pyear}}
GROUP BY c.continent
ORDER BY Population DESC;

After an alias has been declared, type the alias followed by a period—for example c.—to display columns belonging to that table. Continue typing to narrow the list, then use Enter or Tab to accept the selected suggestion.

For a schema-qualified table, typing a schema followed by a period can show tables in that schema. The available suggestions depend on the selected connection and its loaded metadata.

docs.title: Format the query
docs.text:
Select Format to format the current editor content:

  • SQL is indented and its keywords are capitalized.
  • A model query is formatted as DAX.
  • API JSON is syntax-highlighted instead of being treated as SQL.

Formatting changes presentation, not query meaning. It is useful before saving a query or diagnosing a complex join.

docs.title: Use parameters in a query
docs.text:
Parameters are written as double-braced tokens:

WHERE c.year = {{pyear}}
  AND c.continent IN ({{continent}})

Select Param to display the parameter list. From there you can insert a selected parameter into the query, edit it, or create a new parameter. The final replacement text is controlled by the parameter definition, so a parameter may represent a single value, a date, or a complete multi-value SQL fragment.

See Parameters for input controls, list lookups, sheet scope, date and numeric formats, hierarchical selections, and text parsing.

docs.title: Preview parameter substitution
docs.text:
Use Query > Parse query before running when you want to verify the generated statement. Query Tool resolves the parameter tokens, writes the resulting query to the log, and opens the log pane.

This is especially useful for:

  • quoted text values;
  • multi-select IN (...) parameters;
  • optional/None conditions;
  • date formats;
  • finding an unexpected prefix, suffix, separator, or quote.

docs.title: Run a query and limit preview rows
docs.text:
Select Run or press F5. If text is selected in the editor, F5 runs the selected text; otherwise it runs the complete query.

The result appears in the Result pane. The status area and log report progress, warnings, and errors.

Use Settings > Recordcount to change the preview row limit. A smaller limit is useful while developing a query against a large source. The limit controls the Query Tool preview and is not intended as a substitute for a deliberate SQL TOP, LIMIT, or source-side filter when the final definition itself must restrict rows.

docs.title: Log window
docs.text:
Select Log to show or hide the log pane. It contains execution messages, parsed queries, warnings, and errors. When a warning or error occurs, the status area displays a short message and the Log button changes appearance.

Use Settings > Clear log to empty the current log buffer. Clearing the log does not change the query or its result.

A useful diagnostic sequence is:

  1. Clear the log.
  2. Select Parse query to inspect parameter replacement.
  3. Run the query.
  4. Read the new messages without older entries mixed in.

docs.title: Statistics and charts
docs.text:
The Tools menu exposes two related but different views:

  • Statistics opens the chart designer using the query result. This is the same main route as selecting the Chart toolbar button.
  • Show query statistics displays a descriptive statistics table for the returned columns, such as counts and numeric summaries.

If no current result is available, the command runs the query first. Parameters are resolved before the data is handed to the statistics/chart window.

For chart types and formatting, continue to the Chart tool. DAX measures are described separately in DAX measures.

docs.title: Function reference
docs.text:
Select Function to replace the table list with functions supported by the current query mode. Selecting a function shows its description and syntax in the column/details pane. Function help also appears near the editor while entering supported function arguments.

The function list changes with the connection:

Current connection Function family Named SQL source SQL functions appropriate for database queries. Actual database support can vary by provider. table QReports' supported MiniSQL/table functions for querying Excel tables. model DAX functions for Power Pivot model queries.

Do not assume that a function shown for one mode is valid in another. Select the target connection before opening Function.

See Mini SQL for Excel tables for syntax, function groups, examples, the CSV roadmap, and differences from database SQL.

docs.title: Editable query mode
docs.text:
Use Query > Editable query when the result should be edited and written back to a SQL table.

  1. Start with a straightforward query against one updateable SQL table.
  2. Select Editable query.
  3. Edit, add, or delete rows in the Result grid.
  4. Select Save in the result area to write the pending changes.

The source table needs a usable key, and the provider must be able to generate insert, update, and delete commands. Aggregates, calculated columns, joins, and other non-updateable result sets may be displayed but cannot normally be saved back.

In editable mode, Query Tool remembers hidden result columns for the connection/table. Right-click a result header and use Hide this column, Select/hide columns, or Show all columns. Lookup columns can present an ID together with a friendly name while retaining the underlying value; sorting still follows the underlying value.

docs.title: Open and save query files
docs.text:
The File menu supports two useful formats:

  • Open File opens .sql or .qtl files. Recently used files are also tracked by Query Tool.
  • Save as sql file saves only the parameter-resolved SQL text as UTF-8 .sql.
  • Save as qrep file saves a .qtl Query Tool definition containing the raw query, connection, parameters, and measures.

Use .sql when the statement should be portable to another SQL editor. Use .qtl when you want to reopen the complete QReports working definition.

docs.title: Context menus
docs.text: Right-click menus change according to the pane and current connection mode.

docs.title: Table pane
docs.text:
• View top records.
  • Insert the table name or SELECT * into the query.
  • Set a table alias.
  • Add or display join and filter columns in Wizard mode.
  • Edit an updateable table.
  • Show statistics for a table.
  • Automatically size the displayed columns.

docs.title: Column pane
docs.text:
• Insert selected columns into the query.
  • Fill or refresh example values.
  • Show or hide metadata columns such as Alias, Example, Output, Index, Identity, and Type.
  • Expose a filter column.
  • Automatically size the displayed columns.

docs.title: Query editor
docs.text: Select text and right-click to show details for a selected table name, run only the selected area, or copy the selected area.

docs.title: Result pane
docs.text: Right-click a column header to auto-size or hide columns, select visible columns, configure a lookup column, or choose numeric/date formatting. Right-click result cells to copy values or rows and export the visible result to CSV.

docs.title: API tool
docs.text:
Select API tool or Tools > API query to open API Explorer. Existing API JSON in the query editor is passed into the explorer. When you return, the API definition and preview data are passed back through Query Tool so columns, parameters, measures, and the Excel return definition follow the same route as other queries.

See the API tool for the dedicated API workflow.

docs.title: DAX measures
docs.text:
Select Dax or Tools > Define Measures to manage measures associated with the current query definition. Measures are a separate subject because they can include aggregation behavior, calculated columns, formatting, matrix visibility, and model-specific DAX.

Continue to Mini DAX and measures.

docs.title: Power Pivot menu
docs.text:
The Power Pivot menu is relevant primarily when the selected connection is model and the workbook contains a Power Pivot model. Its commands link to Excel's model tools:

  • Manage measures;
  • Manage Relationships;
  • Power Query editor;
  • Open pivot model;
  • View pivot Model as HTML.

These commands depend on an Excel-hosted Query Tool and a workbook/model that supports the requested feature. They may do nothing in the standalone or Canvas-hosted Query Tool.

docs.title: Return the definition
docs.text:
Select Return only after the query and preview are correct. When Query Tool is hosted by Excel, this is the supported route for patching the data-source definition into the sheet without unnecessarily replacing the surrounding setup. Existing measures and other definition elements are carried through the Query Tool workflow.

If Query Tool was opened by Canvas, Statistics, or API Explorer, Return closes Query Tool and passes its current definition back to that caller.

docs.title: Deployment model
docs.text: QReports is published as a VSTO ClickOnce application. setup.exe checks prerequisites and registers the Excel add-in for the current user. The .vsto manifest identifies the application files and published version.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Microsoft Excel desktop on Windows;
  • .NET Framework 4.8;
  • Microsoft Visual Studio Tools for Office Runtime;
  • access to the publication site when installing/updating;
  • access to database/API endpoints configured by the organization.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Close Excel.
  2. Open the approved QReports installation URL.
  3. Run setup.exe.
  4. Accept ClickOnce/VSTO trust prompts allowed by organizational policy.
  5. Open Excel and verify that QRep appears.
  6. Open QRep > Settings > License Status to verify entitlement.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
ClickOnce updates are enabled and the GitHub Pages installation site is the configured source. Excel may check the deployment manifest when the add-in starts. Close all Excel processes before updating so no old assembly remains loaded.

For managed environments, allow-list the publication URL and validate the release signing certificate. Test with the organization's Excel version, bitness, security baseline, and endpoint protection before broad deployment.

docs.title: Troubleshooting deployment
docs.text:
• Check Excel > File > Options > Add-ins for disabled/inactive add-ins.
  • Under Manage: COM Add-ins, verify QReports is enabled.
  • Confirm VSTO Runtime and .NET Framework 4.8 are installed.
  • Close every Excel process and retry.
  • Use QRep > Settings > About to copy environment and assembly-path information.
  • Review Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Remove the add-in
docs.text:
1. Close every Excel window.
  2. Open Windows Settings > Apps > Installed apps or Control Panel > Programs and Features.
  3. Find QReports and choose Uninstall.
  4. Reopen Excel and confirm the QRep Ribbon is gone.

Disabling QReports under Excel COM Add-ins stops it loading but does not remove the ClickOnce installation or local settings.

docs.title: Optional per-user cleanup
docs.text:
Uninstall may intentionally leave configuration and license data. After backing up anything needed, remove these per-user folders if a complete cleanup is required:

%LocalAppData%\QReports
%AppData%\QReports
%AppData%\xlQuery

This deletes local connections, themes, secrets, preferences, history, and the license. Private DPAPI secrets cannot normally be recovered under another Windows account.

Do not remove workbook _control sheets or xlquery definitions unless the reports are also being retired. Uninstalling does not remove definitions saved inside .xlsx or .xlsm files.

docs.title: Reinstallation
docs.text: Reinstall from the approved publication site. Restore only reviewed settings files and recreate private secrets under the Windows account that will run Excel.

docs.title: Data stored in workbooks
docs.text:
QReports definitions normally remain in the workbook alongside the report. Depending on the feature, this can include connection names, query text, API JSON, _control parameters, Mini DAX definitions, and chart/Canvas settings.

Database passwords and API secrets should use the secret store instead of being placed directly in workbook query text or connection JSON.

docs.title: Data stored on the computer
docs.text:
Location Typical content %LocalAppData%\QReports\settings\company Company defaults, themes, shared connection catalog, optional shared secrets. %LocalAppData%\QReports\settings\user User settings, personal connections/themes, private secrets. %AppData%\QReports License, recent query files, lookup definitions, remembered hidden columns. %AppData%\xlQuery Chart specification folder preference. User-selected locations Saved .sql, .qtl, Canvas, chart, CSV, and exported files.

The exact active paths appear in QRep > Settings > About.

docs.title: Credentials and secrets
docs.text:
• Private secrets use Windows DPAPI with CurrentUser scope and are intended for the same Windows user context.
  • Shared secrets use portable obfuscation so a company profile can be copied. This is not strong protection against reverse engineering and is not an enterprise secret vault.
  • Connection definitions can use tokens such as {{secret:key}}; QReports resolves them when the connection/request runs.
  • Prefer private secrets or organization-managed identity for sensitive production access.
  • Restrict settings folders and workbooks according to their data classification.

docs.title: Network activity
docs.text:
Activity Destination/data ClickOnce install/update Manifests and application files from the configured QReports GitHub Pages site. Help button Public documentation in the default browser. Company profile download If automatic profile installation is invoked, a domain manifest and referenced files from the QReports settings site. Manual installation copies local files. Database queries Query and authentication sent to the user/admin-selected database. API queries/authentication Configured request, parameters, headers, body, and authentication sent to configured API/token endpoints.

The current code does not implement a separate telemetry or analytics upload service. Logs remain in application memory unless a user saves or copies them. Database/API use can still transmit workbook-derived values to configured sources, so review those endpoints and queries separately.

docs.title: Security checklist
docs.text:
• Verify release signature and publication URL.
  • Review database and API destinations.
  • Keep sensitive values out of worksheets and query files.
  • Treat shared-secret files as obfuscated, not strongly encrypted.
  • Apply least-privilege database accounts and API scopes.
  • Review workbooks before external sharing because definitions and _control values travel with them.
  • Restrict write access to centrally managed company settings.
  • Confirm proxy, TLS inspection, and firewall rules permit only intended destinations.
  • Test ClickOnce and add-in assemblies with endpoint protection.

docs.title: Logs and support information
docs.text: Logs can contain query text, endpoint errors, names, and parameter-expanded statements. Review them before sharing. About information includes machine, user, domain, paths, version, locale, and display details and should follow the same support-data policy.

docs.title: Technical information
docs.text: This section is intended for IT administrators, security reviewers, and support teams. It describes deployment, local storage, outbound connections, credential handling, and removal.

docs.title: Technical overview
docs.text:
• Product type: Microsoft Excel VSTO add-in for Windows.
  • Deployment: ClickOnce bootstrapper and .vsto manifest.
  • Required framework: .NET Framework 4.8.
  • Required Office component: Visual Studio Tools for Office Runtime.
  • Update source: configured QReports GitHub Pages installation site.
  • Normal installation scope: current Windows user.

Continue with:

  • Installation and updates
  • Local storage and security
  • Uninstall and cleanup

For ordinary end-user setup, use Installation.

docs.title: The QReports ribbon is missing
docs.text:
1. Restart Excel.
  2. Check File → Options → Add-ins.
  3. Confirm that QReports is not disabled.
  4. Reinstall from the published installation page if necessary.

docs.title: An update does not load
docs.text: Close every Excel process before retrying. A running Excel process can retain an older add-in assembly.

docs.title: Getting support
docs.text: When reporting a problem, include the QReports version, Excel version, error message, and the steps required to reproduce it.

docs.title: WebView workspaces
docs.text: QReports now uses a shared WebView2 host for its main interactive tools. The web workspaces use the same visual language, pane behavior, keyboard conventions, connection objects, parameters, and result formatting while keeping the established Excel storage formats.

docs.title: Common layout
docs.text:
• Left panes contain sources, fields, saved objects, or document structure.
  • The centre is the main editor or design surface.
  • Right panes contain properties and supporting tools.
  • Side panes can be resized, collapsed to their edge, and reopened without losing their width.
  • Long-running actions show a loading state. Render-only Canvas refreshes remain off screen.
  • New query and API previews default to 1,000 rows. Existing saved limits are preserved.

docs.title: Query Web
docs.text: Use Query Web to browse schemas, build SQL, edit supported SQL Server tables, run parameterized queries, and inspect Grid, JSON, Parsed SQL, and Messages output. Table and column context menus provide query generation, aliases, distinct-value filters, formatting, column visibility, and previews. The SQL editor supports alias-aware completion and Tab/Shift+Tab indentation for one or several selected lines.

docs.title: API Web
docs.text: API Web separates reusable connections from endpoint definitions. Connections hold the base URL, authentication/workflow, default headers, timeout, and SecretManager references. Endpoints hold method, relative path, request parameters/body, pagination/loop behavior, and response shaping. Use Submitted request to inspect the actual HTTP request without QReports metadata, and Data/Raw response to diagnose the result.

docs.title: Measure workspace
docs.text: Measure workspace creates and validates Mini DAX measures and calculated columns. Right-click a source field for formula templates. Measures support built-in or custom number formats and can be tested in a matrix by dragging fields into Rows, one Columns field, and Values. Load data resolves the current workbook/Canvas parameters before executing the source query.

docs.title: Canvas Web
docs.text: Canvas Web builds pages from table, matrix, chart, card, text, and picture tiles. The report structure and properties panes dock at the sides. Table and Matrix designers use Fields → selected objects/options → Preview. Chart tiles open Chart Web through Design. Returning to Excel or PowerPoint stores the definition with the rendered image.

docs.title: Supporting web forms
docs.text: Parameters, connections and secrets, logs/status, selected-sheet loading, and PowerPoint Canvas-shape selection use focused WebView routes. Secret values are stored through the existing SecretManager and are represented in definitions by tokens instead of clear text.

docs.title: Legacy access
docs.text: The Excel ribbon keeps Legacy tools during the migration period. Use these entries only when comparing behavior or maintaining an older workbook. New workflow buttons open the WebView versions.
